calls.reason: The Feb 1, 2024 Alzahrani et al. preprint found that shuffling answer choices changed the ranking of 5 of 11 models. Swapping choice symbols and changing the scoring method also caused major ranking shifts.

The original controller demonstration could not be checked. GenEval and DEsignBench cover related image-generation weaknesses and strengths but not one-handed design, so the evidence is adjacent and thin.

Carlini et al. support the general point that diffusion models memorise training images. Nothing verifies the controller example he offers as the instance, so the claim as stated is only partly supported.
Lovering and Pavlick link training frequency to failures on reversed relations in one older model, and SeedSelect complicates the inference. Neither establishes his broad causal explanation.
The claim is hedged with 'often'. HRS-Bench shows general instruction-following failures, and NLeseul's own tests had partial successes; neither measures novel, compliant designs.
The claim is hedged ('often seem', 'rumored'). Somepalli et al.'s copying study is narrower and earlier, and no comparison of default and alternative prompts was found.
